problem: The sentence 'One physical qubit now carries the logical qubit in an entangled way' is false and contradicts the whole idea of encoding. No single physical qubit holds the logical qubit; the information is spread across all three, and measuring any one of them destroys it.
fix: The logical qubit is now stored jointly in three physical qubits as α|000>+β|111>. No single qubit carries α or β; the information is in the correlations between the qubits.

problem: Saying the parity observables 'commute with ... the encoded state' is loose: a state is not an operator, so it cannot commute with anything. The reason α and β stay hidden is that both codewords give the same fixed outcome for every parity check.
fix: These observables commute with each other, and both codewords |0_L> and |1_L> give the same outcome (+1) for each of them, so the syndrome is the same for every α and β and reveals nothing about them.
